label: D2 after choosing a2: strong on rare a2->S1, weak late-episode drift on a2->S2
explanation: Fires only at D2 (none at D1, about 6 GO steps). The strongest activations (top quartile, about 0.4-1.0 of max) are a2 followed by a rare transition to S1. That case fires on 100% of its steps and holds about 61% of activation mass, and it is strongest when the agent strongly prefers a2 and S2 is good. It also fires very weakly (about 0.01-0.15 of max) on a2->S2 common D2 steps, almost only in later trials of the episode (ep_trial >= 40, where precision is 0.98). This is a slow drift across the episode, not an event. Late in the episode it also fires weakly on a1->S1 common, so adding that clause raises dev F1 from 0.88 to 0.91; it was left out for simplicity. It never fires on a1->S2 rare or on any rewarded-input (D1) step. Magnitude follows the a2-preference policy logit: most mass is where choice < -4.4. It does not depend on reward, prev_reward or stay. All variables are observable at D2. ep_trial is a proxy for elapsed time in the episode. Dev: P 0.95, R 0.83, F1 0.88, mass recall 0.90.

issues: Some claims check out: the feature fires only at D2 (GO has 6 of 171k active steps, D1 has none). a2->S1 rare has precision 1.0 and holds 61% of activation mass. a1->S2 never fires (precision 0.0). Early-episode a2->S2 (ep_trial<40) almost never fires (precision 0.008).

The label undersells a2->S2. Late a2->S2 (ep_trial>=40) has precision 0.914 and is 51% of all active steps, with 29% of mass, so it is the most common firing case, not a side note. Its strength is also misreported: the profile's top windows show a2->S2c firing at 0.43-0.50 of max, not the claimed 0.01-0.15.

There is a systematic missed class: a1->S1 common late in the episode. The predicate misses 29,674 active steps (17% of active steps, 9.9% of mass), and the misses on both dev and test are nearly all a1->S1c D2 steps, rising slowly across a window (e.g. 0.18 -> 0.19 -> 0.23 -> 0.27). On its own, (phase==D2)&(action==1)&(state==1)&(ep_trial>=80) scores precision 0.991, recall 0.145 (test: 0.992 / 0.142). The explanation mentions this case but leaves it out of the predicate and label, and labels it 'weak' even though it reaches about 0.33 of max.

The late drift starts at different points for the two choices: after about trial 40 for a2 and about trial 80 for a1. So 'late-episode drift on a2->S2' is incomplete; the drift covers common transitions after either choice, starting earlier for a2.
Adding the a1->S1 late clause raises test F1 from 0.882 to 0.959 and mass recall from 0.902 to 0.998, with no loss of precision (0.945). That is too large a gap to treat as optional simplification.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 only: strong after rare a2->S1 (always fires, about 0.4-1.0 of max). Plus a slow drift through the episode on common transitions: a2->S2 after about trial 40 (up to about 0.5 of max), a1->S1 after about trial 80 (up to about 0.3 of max). Never fires on a1->S2.
